# The prelude

The prelude is the part of the standard library every program gets without an import: the files at the top of `runtime/`. Each module after it (`io`, `async`, `json`, ...) is brought in with an import.

- [Built-in functions](internals.md): `assert` and `panic`, which every program can call without an import.
- [Built-in attributes](attributes.md): The built-in attributes, declared as `[Attribute]` structs so a `static` block can read them like its own: `field.has_attribute<Deprecated>()` tests for one and `function.attribute<Deprecated>().message` reads its value (see the reflection chapter).
- [The reflect module (compile time)](reflect.md): `reflect` exists only inside a [`static` block](../language/reflection.md), which runs while compiling.
- [Compiler built-ins](builtins.md): The types and functions the compiler provides itself: raw pointers, weak references, atomics, checked arithmetic and the other `__` intrinsics the runtime is built on.
- [Arguments and exit (deprecated)](process.md): The running program's arguments and exit, kept for the deprecated prelude `arguments()` and `exit()`; the `process` module has them now.
- [String](string.md): A mutable, reference-counted string of UTF-8 text.
- [Numbers](number.md): Reading numbers from text, and arithmetic that says what to do on overflow.
- [Ranges](range.md): Ranges of numbers: `a..b` and `a..>b`.
- [Array](array.md): A growable, contiguous, zero-indexed sequence of `T` values.
- [HashMap and HashSet](hash.md): Hashing: `hash<T>(value)`, the 64-bit hash `HashMap` and `HashSet` use for their keys, and the hash maps and sets themselves.
- [Map and Set](map.md): Sorted collections: `Map<K, V>` and `Set<K>`, kept in key order on a red-black tree, and `compare<T>`, the ordering they sort keys by.
- [OrderedMap](ordered_map.md): `OrderedMap<K, V>`: a hash map that keeps its keys in the order they were first inserted.
- [Iterators](iterator.md): Something a `for` loop can step through, one element at a time.
- [Scoped](scoped.md): The scope protocol behind `with (var x = scope) { ... } else { ... }`.
- [Weak](weak.md): Weak references: `Weak<T>` points at an object without keeping it alive.
- [Handle](handle.md): `Handle<T>`: owns a resource that Pepper's reference counting does not know about, such as a C library's object, and releases it when the last reference to the handle goes away, like C#'s `SafeHandle`.
- [Result](result.md): `Result<T, E>`: the value of an operation that can fail, either `Ok` holding its value or `Err` holding its error, like Rust's `Result`.
- [Optional](optional.md): A value of type `T` that may be absent: either Value, holding a `T`, or Empty, holding nothing, like Rust's `Option<T>` and Swift's `Optional`.
- [Copying](copy.md): Deep copies: `copy(value)` makes a copy that shares no object that is not thread-safe with the original, so it can be handed to another thread; `Copyable<T>` lets a type say how it is copied.
- [URI](uri.md): URI references (RFC 3986): parse any URI, such as `https://example.com/a?b#c`, `mailto:someone@example.com` or `/items?page=2`, into its parts.
- [Test checks](expect.md): Checks for tests: `expect_equal`, `expect_not_equal`, `expect_true` and `expect_false`, which every program can call without an import.
